basic_info: 45-year-old female presenting with a diagnosis of hepatitis C, reported by primary care physician; patient is asymptomatic and previously unaware of the condition.
present_illness: Patient is asymptomatic but was recently diagnosed with hepatitis C by her primary care physician. The diagnosis was made based on recent blood work, though the exact date of diagnosis is unknown. The patient has no prior history of hepatitis C or treatment. The patient reports feeling fatigued at the end of the day, even though she gets enough sleep. The fatigue has been ongoing for a few months and is described as mild to moderate in severity. No other symptoms such as nausea, weight loss, changes in bowel habits, or jaundice have been reported.
past_history: No prior illnesses, operations, or trauma reported. No known allergies. No family history of liver disease or hepatitis mentioned. The patient is not aware of having been tested for hepatitis B or E. Risk factors for hepatitis C include a history of intravenous drug use (ceased 15 years ago), multiple sexual partners, and no known blood transfusions or recent medical procedures involving blood exposure.
aux_exam: Hepatitis C antibody test was positive; HCV RNA test has not been performed yet. No liver function tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin, albumin) or imaging studies have been conducted.
